summary: Brick 1857 light at the south tip of Dutch Island, marking Dutch Island Harbor in Narragansett Bay; automated 1947, deactivated 1979, state-owned and not open to visitors.

structures.note: Three-story brick tower, 13 feet square in plan, attached to the keeper's dwelling (NRHP); 35 ft base to lantern (USLHS).
Two-story brick Greek Revival keeper's dwelling attached to the tower; torn down after automation in 1947.
Boathouse built 1867 and destroyed by a storm two years later; later boathouses 1894 and 1939 (NRHP).

access.note: Tower not open to the public; the tourism listing says it is best seen by boat. The archive lists the station as open to the public; the 1980s nomination said accessible, unrestricted. Sources differ.

visit.note: Tourism listing: not open to the public, best seen by boat.

corrections.why: Deactivated 1979 (NRHP nomination; USLHS 'Year Discontinued: 1979'); the record's 'active' is wrong.
USLHS gives 35 feet (10.7 m) from base to lantern; the NRHP's 13 feet is the tower's square width, so 13.0 m looks like a width read as a height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS record says the station was established in 1826; the NRHP nomination says the state ceded the land in 1825 and the light was first lit on 1 January 1827, and it calls the station established in 1827. The story gives both; the facts use the nomination's first-lit date.

The Archive lists the station as open to the public, the 1980s nomination says accessible and unrestricted, and the tourism listing says the lighthouse is not open to the public and is best seen by boat. Not resolved; the facts record it as restricted and the story says the sources differ.

notes_for_editor: Corrected 2026-10-22 on page images: the 1892 Plum Beach passage ('extreme danger of grounding on Plum Beach', 'recent grounding of the steamer Pequot') is printed p. 64 (scan 403); the 1900 boundary-post entry (item 197) is printed p. 62 (scan 73), not scan 74 as the corpus label said. 1893-94 'New boatways' entry (scan 371): printed page not confirmed; cited by scan page only. Wreck date: the Providence News of 22 Jan 1903 says the Seaboard put in 'yesterday' (21 Jan) and ran into the ledge 'a few minutes after noon'; the earlier draft's 'night' was wrong. The OCR is poor in places (the bow distance reads 'scarce 30 feat'); the story gives 'about 30 feet' without quoting it. The paper names no keeper; Albert H. Porter is the roster keeper for 1901-1915, which covers the date, and the story says so. Keeper roster: the USLHS page lists 22 entries as printed; Robert Dennis appears twice (1843 and 1846-1853); Marion Fife is under the '1st Assistant Lighthouse Keeper' heading; Thomas Coggeshall (contractor) has no years and is not in the story. Record conflicts: characteristic 'Fl(2+1) R 6s' in the record is not supported by the nomination (a fixed white light when active); left out. Range: the nomination says the fixed white light could be seen for eleven miles (not converted, left out); the record's 4.0 nm has no support. Structure height: record 13.0 m is the square width in feet; proposed correction to 10.7 m (35 ft base to lantern, USLHS). Access: the Archive says open to the public; the 1980s nomination says accessible and unrestricted; the Visit Rhode Island listing says not open to the public and best seen by boat. Not resolved; the story states the disagreement. The 1979 deactivation and the 1947 automation are from the nomination and the Archive. Verification: 2026-10-22 fact-check; the nomination was read in full; Visit Rhode Island and the 1903 article were read from the cached pages.
